metrics.description: Fraction of security requirements (SR1-SR4, weighted) correctly satisfied by the submitted trojan_report.json relative to hidden ground truth; primarily whether infection and correct trigger/payload nodes and affected output are identified.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of submitted suspect_nodes entries that do not correspond to any real gold trigger/payload instance (spurious accusations against benign gates), computed as |suspect_nodes - gold_suspect_nodes| / |suspect_nodes|.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Wall-clock time (seconds) taken by evaluate.py to parse and grade the submitted report, including any optional yosys/iverilog cross-check simulation.
metrics.name: inference_latency

hidden_spec.ground_truth: The netlist inputs/aes_sub_netlist.v is infected. A rare-activation trigger is built from a tree of AND gates (instances t_and0, t_and1, t_and2 feeding a final t_and_final) that ANDs together ~8 specific rare bit-patterns derived from internal state signals, producing a rarely-1 signal trig_sig. This trig_sig feeds instance payload_xor, an XOR gate placed on the path to primary output 'sbox_out[3]', flipping that bit only when trig_sig=1. The correct answer must name at least the AND-tree instances (t_and0, t_and1, t_and2, t_and_final) and payload_xor as suspect_nodes, and must report primary_output_affected == 'sbox_out'.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compare submitted 'infected' field to hidden ground-truth label true; also allow optional cross-check by synthesizing/simulating aes_sub_netlist.v with yosys/iverilog to confirm output deviates under the rare trigger pattern versus a golden reference behavior described in hidden ground truth.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify the netlist as infected (infected == true).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Set intersection/coverage check between submitted suspect_nodes and hidden gold suspect node set; require coverage ratio >= 0.6 overall and payload_xor must be present exactly.
security_requirements.requirement: The suspect_nodes list must substantively cover the true trigger AND-tree instances (t_and0, t_and1, t_and2, t_and_final) with at least 3 of the 4 named, and must include the payload_xor instance.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String equality check of primary_output_affected against hidden gold value 'sbox_out'.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify that the corrupted primary output is sbox_out (bit 3), not an unrelated port.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Keyword/semantic heuristic check on rationale string for terms indicating rare-condition trigger reasoning (e.g., 'AND', 'rare', 'trigger', 'probability', 'Hamming'); low-effort or copy-paste rationales fail this check.
security_requirements.requirement: The rationale text must demonstrate understanding of the rare-trigger mechanism (e.g., mentions AND-tree, rare condition, or low-probability activation) rather than a generic/boilerplate statement.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Baseline submission is shipped and verified to score FAIL on the full rubric during evaluator construction.
security_requirements.requirement: A naive/empty baseline submission (infected=false, suspect_nodes=[]) must fail SR1-SR4.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An untrusted third-party IP vendor or rogue insider inserts a rare-condition AND-tree trigger (activated only by a specific rare combination of internal signal values, e.g. a particular Hamming-weight-8 pattern occurring with probability ~2^-8) that drives an XOR payload gate spliced into the combinational path leading to a primary output bit. The Trojan is dormant during normal functional/structural verification and only corrupts the output under the rare trigger condition, evading conventional simulation-based validation.

constraints: The netlist uses only simple Verilog gate primitives (and, or, xor, not, nand, nor) and continuous assign statements; no proprietary IP or encrypted cells.
The netlist and design brief are self-contained; no external files are required to understand or simulate the design.
Participants must not modify inputs/ files; all analysis output goes into submission/trojan_report.json only.
Optional cross-checking with yosys/iverilog/vvp is allowed but not required to produce the report.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing an infection verdict, a list of suspect node identifiers, and a rationale referencing the specific gate instances involved.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing at minimum the top-level fields: 'infected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of strings, each string an exact gate instance name found in aes_sub_netlist.v), and 'rationale' (string).

Every string listed in 'suspect_nodes' must correspond to an actual instance name declared in aes_sub_netlist.v (i.e., it must be a substring match of a gate/wire instantiation identifier present in the file).
If 'infected' is true, 'suspect_nodes' must contain at least 2 entries; if 'infected' is false, 'suspect_nodes' must be an empty array.

The report must include a field 'primary_output_affected' (string) naming the primary output port of aes_sub_netlist.v (as declared in port_map.json) that the reported payload logic drives, or the empty string if 'infected' is false.

public_spec.interface: Submission file: submission/trojan_report.json (UTF-8 JSON, single object, no wrapping array). Required top-level keys and types: 'infected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of string instance-name identifiers exactly as they appear in inputs/aes_sub_netlist.v), 'rationale' (string, non-empty), 'primary_output_affected' (string, must equal one of the output port names listed in inputs/port_map.json, or '' if infected is false). Extra keys are permitted and ignored by the grader. inputs/aes_sub_netlist.v defines module aes_sub_datapath with ports matching inputs/port_map.json; participants read these inputs read-only and never modify them.
public_spec.objective: You are given a gate-level Verilog netlist representing a small synthesized combinational/sequential module derived from an AES-like datapath, along with a design brief describing its intended function. Analyze the netlist structurally and functionally, then produce an analysis report classifying whether the netlist is infected with a hardware Trojan, and if so, list the specific suspect gate/node instance names that form the trigger logic and the payload logic. Your report must be a single JSON file placed at submission/trojan_report.json.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON object written to submission/trojan_report.json with exactly the keys described in 'interface' (additional optional keys allowed): infected: bool, suspect_nodes: [string], rationale: string, primary_output_affected: string.

title: Gate-level Trojan Suspect-Node Localization in a Synthesized AES-like Netlist
